brief: Kosovo's audit and assurance layer for banking has three distinct, well-populated channels plus one weak spot. The strongest and most under-exploited is the supervisory/professional register axis: BQK approves and — per its own external-auditor regulation — registers the auditors allowed to audit licensed banks, MFIs, payment and e-money institutions, while KKRF (under Law 06/L-032) licenses statutory auditors and audit firms and SCAAK publishes a paginated, enumerable directory of accounting and auditing firms plus lists of certified auditors; together these give a near-complete actor map, though neither official register's live URL was pinned down in this pass. The second channel is firm-published and issuer-published disclosure: PwC Kosovo and Grant Thornton Kosovo publish multi-year statutory transparency reports (Deloitte Kosova likewise), while banks such as BKT, BpB, İşbank branch, Raiffeisen Kosovo and NLB host full signed independent auditor's reports as year-stamped PDFs in Albanian and English — the richest per-institution evidence of auditor identity, opinion type and IFRS/ECL language. The third is oversight from outside the sector: ZKA (the National Audit Office, publishing in sq, sr and en) audits budget organisations and publicly owned enterprises and reports one day after submission, the Ministry of Economy's POE unit publishes POE auditor reports, and the World Bank CFRR's Kosovo A&A ROSC benchmarks how much a Kosovo audit opinion is worth. The weak spot is advisory content: no Kosovo-specific Big Four banking-sector survey or outlook was found, KPMG and EY Kosovo entities could not be confirmed at all, and Serbian-language material exists only where official bodies publish bilingually.
